HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Garden Tools — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the garden’s team: five tools, each with a one-job rule, and the trowel handed to the child as their very own shovel.

What is this?

The garden runs on its tools: the shovel digs deep, the rake gathers, the trowel plants, the gloves guard the hands, the wheelbarrow hauls it all.

What does it mean?

Real tools, honestly given, are how children join the work. A child with their own trowel is not watching gardening — the child is gardening.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card and the real tools. The digging job is one pot or one small patch: trowel, hole, seed or seedling, done. Gloves go on first, every time — that is the ritual.

Why this matters

The yard-garden word rides along quietly: US families say yard, UK families say garden, the tools are identical. The one-job rule (shovels dig, rakes gather) is the lesson’s spine.

What it teaches

Tool discipline (one job each), fine and gross motor work (trowel grip, rake pull), and the sequence of planting — dig, place, cover, water.

Words to learn

shovelraketrowelgardening gloveswheelbarrowgardenyard

Say this to your child

“"Garden tools! Shovel digs, rake gathers, trowel plants — the trowel is YOUR little shovel. Gloves on, one hole to dig, and the wheelbarrow waits for its driver."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card outside: "the garden has a tool team — gloves first."
  2. Gloves on: the ritual that says work is beginning — wiggle each finger home.
  3. Meet the big tools by sight: the shovel digs deep holes, the rake gathers leaves — rrrike.
  4. The trowel is yours: one pot, one small hole, one seedling or seed in, soil patted down.
  5. Wheelbarrow finale: load the pots or leaves in, and the child takes one ride as the foreman.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Garden Tools" sit over a blue shovel, a rake, a hand trowel, a pair of cream gardening gloves and a blue wheelbarrow with one wheel.

Ask your child

"Which tool digs the small holes?" (the trowel) "What do we put on first?" (the gloves) "Which tool carries everything?" (the wheelbarrow)

What your child can say or do

Your child might sleep with the trowel, rake every leaf in the postcode into one noble pile, or ride the wheelbarrow and refuse to disembark.

Out in the real world

Community gardens, farms and grandma’s yard all run the same team. The child who knows trowel from shovel is handed real jobs at every garden gate.

Try it together

Tool Race (gentle edition): three picture cards — shovel, rake, trowel — and three jobs called out. The child runs to touch the right real tool. Digging bonus: one real hole in one real pot, dug entirely by them.

Staying safe

Tools are for their jobs and only their jobs, and the pointy ends stay down and away. The wheelbarrow ride happens with a grown-up steering. Gloves are the ritual that starts every session.

This lesson pairs with the Garden Tools flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
